record.paper_title: Selected open problems in Matching Under Preferences
record.original_question: For the general (a, b)-supermatch notion in Stable Marriage or Stable Roommates instances with incomplete lists, determine whether the decision problem “does there exist an (a, b)-supermatch?” belongs to NP.

evidence.quote: However, for the more general case of (a, b)-supermatches, it is not even known whether the problem belongs to NP.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Consider a Stable Marriage with Incomplete lists (SMI) instance, or more generally a Stable Roommates with Incomplete lists (SRI) instance: there is a finite set of agents, each of whom ranks a subset of the other agents in strict order of preference. A matching M is a set of acceptable pairs such that each agent appears in at most one pair. A pair (x,y) not in M blocks M if x and y find each other acceptable and each of x,y is either unmatched in M or strictly prefers the other to their current partner. M is stable if it has no blocking pair.

Given two nonnegative integers a and b, a stable matching M is called an (a,b)-supermatch if, for every subset S of at most a pairs in M, removing these pairs (so that the 2|S| agents involved become single) can be "repaired" by producing a new stable matching M' such that:
 (i) every agent in S is matched in M' (possibly to a different partner), and
 (ii) M' differs from M\S in at most b additional pairs (i.e., apart from the pairs in S being replaced, at most b other pairs of M are modified).

Question. Determine whether the following decision problem belongs to the complexity class NP: given an SMI (or SRI) instance and integers a, b, does there exist an (a,b)-supermatch?

Equivalently: is there a polynomial-size certificate, verifiable in polynomial time, witnessing the existence of an (a,b)-supermatch for arbitrary a (in particular a > 1)?
artifact.status_search_result: Published complexity studies on robust stable marriage establish NP-completeness of the (1,b)-supermatch decision problem, but for general a > 1 the membership of the (a,b)-supermatch existence problem in NP remains unresolved: no polynomial-time verifiable certificate is known. The problem is NP-hard but not known to be in NP.

status_evidence.title: Complexity Study for the Robust Stable Marriage Problem
status_evidence.snippet: (1,1)- and (1,b)-supermatch decision problems are NP-complete; membership in NP for general (a,b) with a>1 is not established.
status_evidence.claim: For a>1, whether the (a,b)-supermatch existence problem is in NP is open.

status_evidence.title: On the Complexity of Robust Stable Marriage
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes NP-completeness of (1,b)-supermatch existence; leaves general (a,b) case unresolved regarding NP membership.
status_evidence.claim: General (a,b)-supermatch problem is NP-hard but NP membership remains open.
